sections.h2: Where is Fall River and what is the land like?
sections.html:
Fall River is a city in Bristol County on the eastern shore of Mount Hope Bay, at the mouth of the Taunton River, against the Rhode Island line. The 2020 census counted 94,000 residents, making it the tenth-largest city in Massachusetts.

The city has 40.2 square miles in total, with more than seven square miles of that water. Much of it is built on hillsides that rise sharply from the shore to more than 200 feet, and Copicut Hill, the highest point, tops 404 feet. A seller on the hill and a seller near the water face different driveways, different drainage and different foundations.

sections.h2: How did the mills shape Fall River housing?
sections.html:
Fall River was one of the leading textile centers in the country, and its houses came with the mills. By 1868 it had passed Lowell as the top textile city in America, and the city was second in the world only to Manchester, England, in output by 1876.

To house the workers, over 12,000 units of company housing were built. Wikipedia describes thousands of wood-framed, multi-family tenements, often three-floor triple-deckers with up to six apartments. Many are still standing, and many are now owned by people who live in one unit and rent the others, or by heirs who never planned to be landlords.

Granite from local quarries built many of the mills and some homes. The population peaked at 120,485 in 1920 and the first wave of mill closures came in 1923.

sections.h2: How has Fall River's population changed?
sections.html:
Fall River grew from about 12,000 people when it became a city in 1854 to a peak of 120,485 in 1920. The 2020 census counted 94,000.

The state line was settled in 1861 when the U.S. Supreme Court moved the Rhode Island boundary to what is now State Avenue, joining the two parts of Fall River into one Massachusetts city. A 1843 fire destroyed much of the town center, and the city's motto, We'll Try, dates to its aftermath.

sections.h2: What is Fall River's economy today?
sections.html:
The textile industry moved on long ago, but its buildings remain. These institutions and sites are named on the city's Wikipedia page:

  • Battleship Cove, home to the world's largest collection of World War II naval vessels, including the battleship USS Massachusetts
  • Bristol Community College, founded in 1965
  • Two University of Massachusetts Dartmouth sites in the city
  • B.M.C. Durfee High School and Diman Regional Vocational Technical High School
  • Fall River Heritage State Park on the waterfront

Wikipedia does not list the largest private employers, so ask the city or its chamber of commerce for current employment figures.

sections.h2: Which roads and bridges serve Fall River?
sections.html:
Interstate 195 is the main east-west route, entering the city over the Charles M. Braga Jr. Memorial Bridge and continuing through the middle of the city to Westport. The bridge opened in 1966 as a six-lane cantilever truss span about 1.2 miles long.

Six other routes also serve the city: Route 6, MA 138, MA 79, MA 81, MA 177 and MA 24. The highway reaches New Bedford and Cape Cod to the east and Providence to the west, which makes Fall River workable for commuters into Rhode Island. The Route 79 viaduct was demolished in 2014 and replaced with a surface boulevard. Fall River's city hall is built over the interstate.

sections.h2: What water and weather issues affect a Fall River house?
sections.html:
Fall River has a long shoreline, a river and large ponds, so water is part of the city's geography. The Quequechan River falls 128 feet in its last half mile, and during the 1960s Interstate 195 was routed along it with a section carried underground in culverts.

The North Watuppa Pond is the city's main reservoir, and a large forested watershed lies east of it. Ask the city or your insurance agent for the flood zone of your parcel before you list, since buyers and lenders will.

sections.h2: What schools and colleges are in Fall River?
sections.html:
Fall River Public Schools runs every public school in the city and has one public high school, B.M.C. Durfee High School. Diman Regional Vocational Technical High School serves Fall River, Somerset, Swansea and Westport.

The city also has private and parish schools, including six Catholic schools, and Atlantis Charter School, a pre-K to 8 school with a marine science theme founded in 1995. Bishop Connolly High School closed in May 2023. Espirito Santo School opened in 1910 as the first Portuguese grammar school in the United States, which reflects the Portuguese culture that Wikipedia says the city is known for.

Bristol Community College, founded in 1965, and two University of Massachusetts Dartmouth sites give the city a base of students and staff. The main public library opened in 1899 on North Main Street, built from local granite.

sections.h2: How are Fall River property taxes handled at sale?
sections.html:
Property taxes in Massachusetts are assessed locally, and your bill shows the due dates. Under the state Appellate Tax Board guide, quarterly bills are generally due August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1, and the abatement application is due by the first installment.

Assessments reflect value as of January 1 before the fiscal year. If you think your house is overvalued, the guide says you must show fair cash value is lower than the assessed value, and comparable sales help.

sections.h2: What does Massachusetts require before a Fall River sale closes?
sections.html:
Your local fire department must issue a certificate of compliance for smoke and carbon monoxide alarms. The state advises scheduling the inspection once the closing date is set, and a fee applies.

Battery smoke alarms older than ten years need to be replaced with sealed ten-year photoelectric alarms. A multi-unit building has more alarms to check, so start early. The deed is also subject to the state's deed excise under chapter 64D, and your attorney will include it on the closing statement.

sections.h2: What local rules should a Fall River seller ask about?
sections.html:
Questions about rental registration, building permits for past work, code enforcement and any open violations belong with city departments.

Before listing a multi-family building, ask City Hall whether any permits were left open, whether the number of units matches city records, and whether the property has any outstanding orders. A buyer's attorney will ask the same questions, and clearing them early avoids a delay at the closing table.

sections.h2: What are the options for selling a triple-decker or other Fall River house?
sections.html:
You can list the property, sell it on your own, or take a cash offer. A triple-decker with tenants in place or a house that needs a roof can be slow to sell through a listing.

  • Listing suits a clean, vacant house with time to spare.
  • A cash offer suits inherited, tenant-occupied or run-down property.
  • Selling by owner suits a seller comfortable with contracts.

faqs.q: What county is Fall River in?
faqs.a: Fall River is in Bristol County, Massachusetts, on Mount Hope Bay beside the Rhode Island line.

faqs.q: How many people live in Fall River?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 94,000 residents, and the Census Bureau estimate for July 2025 is 95,298.

faqs.q: Can I sell a triple-decker in Fall River with tenants?
faqs.a: Yes. Tenants' rights continue after a sale, so tell the buyer about leases and rents. A cash buyer can purchase an occupied building as is.

faqs.q: Do I need a smoke and CO certificate in Fall River?
faqs.a: Yes. Massachusetts requires one from the local fire department for a sale or transfer of a home, and the department charges a fee.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Fall River assessment?
faqs.a: File an abatement application with the assessors by the first installment due date on your bill. If denied, appeal to the Appellate Tax Board within three months.
